workflows.name: Quick answer
workflows.trigger: A question one bounded read answers: one file or symbol, one ticket, one message, one doc
needs: The connection that holds the answer

endpoints.outcome: A marked reply that names what it read
endpoints.when: The read answers the question

endpoints.outcome: A reaction, or no reply
endpoints.when: The message asks nothing of you, as most messages in a watched channel don't

endpoints.outcome: The clone answers what it can and passes the rest to you
endpoints.when: More is needed and the asker may not ask for work

workflows.name: Research
workflows.trigger: A question that needs more than a quick read: tracing behaviour, comparing versions or dates, a failure, sources that disagree
needs: For an incident, read access to that environment's logs and data

endpoints.outcome: An answer from the worker's report, with its sources and what stays uncertain
endpoints.when: The worker could read what it needed

endpoints.outcome: The change goes on to delivery
endpoints.when: The report shows a change is needed

endpoints.outcome: A blocked report, and you hear which connection to reconnect
endpoints.when: A sign-in is missing or expired, or the worker lacks access

workflows.name: Your change to a document or ticket
workflows.trigger: Your own message, in your self-DM or with your icon, asks to create or change a Doc, Sheet, ticket or page
needs: Google, or Jira and Confluence, on Set up

endpoints.outcome: The change, and a reply saying what changed
endpoints.when: Your message in that turn asked for it

endpoints.outcome: Nothing changes, and the clone passes it on or asks you to ask in a message of your own
endpoints.when: Someone else asked, or the request came from an earlier turn

workflows.name: Delivery
workflows.trigger: A request for a change that makes sense and needs nothing more from you
needs: Jira and Confluence on Set up
OpenCode signed in to OpenAI, for the GPT reviews

projectCommands.name: create-ticket
projectCommands.role: Writes the ticket when the repository has it; otherwise a worker writes one

projectCommands.name: execute
projectCommands.role: Implements, has GPT review the pull request, merges, deploys to dev and checks the change there; used only where the repository may merge

workflows.review: GPT reviews a ticket the workflow wrote or rewrote, and the pull request. While GPT is unavailable the review waits; Claude never reviews in its place.

endpoints.outcome: A reviewed pull request, not merged
endpoints.when: The repository may not merge, or it has no execute command

endpoints.outcome: Merged, deployed to dev and checked there
endpoints.when: The repository may merge and has an execute command

endpoints.outcome: The review waits
endpoints.when: OpenCode is not signed in to OpenAI, or GPT is out of usage

endpoints.outcome: A reviewed, green pull request waits to merge
endpoints.when: A breaking change must land after another service's change, which its requester times

endpoints.outcome: Delivery stops, and the thread hears who has the ticket
endpoints.when: The ticket is assigned to someone other than you, or lost the auto label it was taken with

endpoints.outcome: A short ticket for the colleague instead of a change
endpoints.when: The change is in a colleague's repository and they have not approved it in their own message

endpoints.outcome: A one-line refusal
endpoints.when: The request is for staging, production, a release, or someone else's branch

endpoints.outcome: A question to you
endpoints.when: Ticket review findings remain after two rounds or are disputed, or a product or scope decision is missing

workflows.name: Dependency updates
workflows.trigger: A request to work through dependency pull requests, a security update or a version bump
needs: OpenCode signed in to OpenAI, for the GPT reviews
workflows.review: GPT reviews every pull request on its current head before it merges, an unchanged bot pull request included. While GPT is unavailable it waits; Claude never reviews in its place.

endpoints.outcome: Merged one at a time, each deploy to dev checked
endpoints.when: The repository may merge, the update carries no danger flag and every check passed

endpoints.outcome: A reviewed pull request, not merged
endpoints.when: The repository may not merge, or the merge would deploy beyond dev

endpoints.outcome: A report: merged, flagged and open pull requests, where each merge reached, checks still open, and proposals for new features and deprecations
endpoints.when: The run ends

endpoints.outcome: The pull request waits for its review
endpoints.when: OpenCode is not signed in to OpenAI, or GPT is out of usage

endpoints.outcome: The queue stops until the cause is known
endpoints.when: A deploy or a check after a merge fails

endpoints.outcome: The update is flagged for you with its evidence and options
endpoints.when: It is dangerous: a major version of auth, payment, data or framework code, a runtime change, a breaking change no test covers, several majors at once, or a supply-chain change such as a new publisher

endpoints.outcome: Yours to do
endpoints.when: Closing a pull request, telling the bot to ignore a version, or turning a proposal into a ticket
